Subject: HarborWell — post-call: residency & air-gapped constraints (next steps)

Hi Alice / Derek —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the concrete asks I captured so we can stay aligned while we pull the technical pack together. I tried to keep this short — call out anything I missed or corrected below.

High-level goal
- Run Redwood Inference in a private/on-prem environment for PII processing of clinical intake forms and care logs. Objective: keep inference hosts behind HarborWell network boundaries; no customer data leaves your VPC or on-prem cluster.

Primary pain points / constraints you emphasized
- Air-gap / closed-network requirement: model hosts must not initiate outbound connections to the public internet. Any control-plane connectivity must be customer-provided and approved.
- Data residency: all inference logs and payloads must remain in HarborWell-managed infra in us-east-1 or on-prem datacenter (no cross-region replication).
- Key management: encryption keys must be held in your HSM/KMS. Redwood must integrate with your KMS via a private connector (no external key staging).
- Audit & retention: security needs 7+ year audit logs; explainability traces preferred but currently scoped to metadata-only retention.
- Allowed egress: anything that needs updates (models, security signatures) should happen via an approved egress proxy; timeboxed, scheduled, and audited.

What we (Redwood) proposed on the call
- Private deployment with a customer-managed private control plane: we can ship a self-hosted control plane that runs in your VPC or on-prem enclave and talks to model hosts over internal networking.
- Model variants: we’ll recommend smaller quantized variants for inference to meet latency & cost targets; can pin exact model versions for production.
- KV/prefix caching and batching will be configured to run entirely inside your network to avoid outgoing calls.

Immediate asks / open items for HarborWell (action items for your security & infra teams)
1) Share your current VPC/network diagram and any firewall/proxy egress policies (attachment: harborwell_network_map_v1.pdf).
2) Provide list of allowed IP ranges and the proposed method for key provisioning to HSM/KMS.
3) Confirm whether a bastion or jump-host pattern is acceptable for scheduled software pulls, or whether you require removable media/manual updates for model binaries.
4) Timeline: you mentioned procurement window in late Q3 — can you confirm target date for a pilot?

What we’ll deliver (action items from Redwood)
- On-prem playbook draft covering air-gap deployment options and controls (will attach initial playbook).
- Short risk matrix mapping the items above to our mitigations (HSM integrations, no-Internet runtime, local logs).
- SOW skeleton and an initial runbook for the pilot (attached: sow_outline_2027.docx).

Proposed next steps
- Technical deep-dive with HarborWell infra + security (60–90m) to walk the network map and agree on allowed egress patterns.
- Prep session w/ your security to review the KMS/HSM flow and key lifecycle.

Proposed times (pick one):
- Tue May 4, 10:00–11:30 ET
- Wed May 5, 14:00–15:30 ET

I’ll hold both tentative slots; if those don’t work send three alternatives.

Attachments: harborwell_network_map_v1.pdf, sow_outline_2027.docx

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Corrections / clarifications
- The environment will be a hybrid: primary must be on-prem in our Boston DC (we label that HW-BOS-01) with a DR replica in us-east-1 that we control — but replication windows must be manually initiated.
- We cannot accept automatic outbound model updates. Patch and model pulls must be via our secure pull server (we’ll provide access details).
- KMS: we’ll provide a key-wrapping endpoint hosted on-prem; the HSM team will not allow external-shaped key material.

Security will send the following by EOD Thu: VPC diagram in the HarborWell template, a CSV of allowed egress destinations (very small list), and our standard security questionnaire (attached).

Procurement note: procurement is aiming for pilot approval by Sep 30, 2027.

We’re available for the technical deep-dive: Wed May 5, 14:00–15:30 ET works for the infra team. Please send an invite and call agenda.
